slides.notes: Options: A) A topic: one subject in a Theme folder (haipipe-block today); B) A stage: one step of a pipeline, b00 raw to b31 endpoint (pipeline-blocks.md); C) A promise to one reader: one delivery, and the Questions it must answer for that reader. Leaning: the third; the first two are ways the work was cut. Still open: Does a data stage have a reader? Maybe the next Block is its reader.
slides.content:
Headline (top-left, large): "A Block is a promise to one reader?"
Three option cards across the middle, joined by a wavy line:
 Card A, label "A topic": a folder with a tag; caption "one subject in a folder"
 Card B, label "A stage": three boxes joined by arrows, lettered "raw", "records", "cases"; caption "one step of a pipeline"
 Card C, label "A promise", circled with a thick orange marker loop and a small hand-written tag "leaning": a person receiving a parcel that holds question marks; caption "one delivery, the questions it must answer"
Bottom-right mustard sticky note with a big question mark: "Still open: does a data stage have a reader?"
Focal point: card C.

slides.notes: Options: A) Questions are the parts: Status counts answers (what the page did); B) Jobs are the parts; Questions are the contract that Jobs answer (answers: Q01); C) Fold Questions into Jobs: one Job, one question as its goal. Leaning: the second. Still open: What about a Job that serves every Question, like j01's shared tables?
slides.content:
Headline (top-left, large): "Jobs are the parts, Questions the contract?"
Three option cards across the middle, joined by a wavy line:
 Card A, label "Questions": a checklist with three ticked lines; caption "the parts are the questions"
 Card B, label "Jobs + Questions", circled with a thick orange marker loop and a small hand-written tag "leaning": two gears, each tied by a dotted thread to a question-mark card; caption "Jobs do the work, each answers a Question"
 Card C, label "One each": one gear glued to one question card; caption "one Job, one question"
Bottom-right mustard sticky note with a big question mark: "Still open: a Job that serves every Question?"
Focal point: card B.

slides.notes: Options: A) The plan stage, before Work; B) A separate place to think, beside Report and Work; C) The discussion itself: rounds (sessions, meetings) that loop through Work and Report and come back. Leaning: the third. Still open: Does every session need a home topic, named at its start?
slides.content:
Headline (top-left, large): "A Studio is the conversation itself?"
Three option cards across the middle, joined by a wavy line:
 Card A, label "A plan": a folded map with a pin; caption "the step before Work"
 Card B, label "A room": an open door; caption "a place beside Report and Work"
 Card C, label "The talk", circled with a thick orange marker loop and a small hand-written tag "leaning": three speech bubbles in a circle with a looping arrow; caption "rounds that loop through Work and Report"
Bottom-right mustard sticky note with a big question mark: "Still open: does every session need a home topic?"
Focal point: card C.

slides.idea: How does a round leave the Studio?
slides.notes: Options: A) To Work: a decision starts a Job, a Task or a Run; B) To Report: a decision answers a Question; C) Back to the Studio: what is still open becomes the next round. Still open: Should a Run card point back to the round that started it (from: s04 p02)?
slides.content:
Headline (top-left, large): "Every round leaves the Studio three ways"
Centre-left: a cloud-shaped doodle labelled "Studio round", with a small speech bubble and a pencil inside. Three sketchy arrows go out of it:
 arrow 1 (sage green) to a hammer and gears, label "Work", small handwriting "a decision starts a Job"
 arrow 2 (light blue) to an open notebook with a tick, label "Report", small handwriting "a decision answers a Question"
 arrow 3 (soft orange) curls back into the cloud, label "Next round", small handwriting "what is still open"
Bottom-right mustard sticky note with a big question mark: "Still open: should a Run point back to its round?"
Focal point: the cloud.

slides.idea: If you keep only one screen of a Block
slides.notes: Options: A) The Mindmap: how it is built; B) The Findings: what it found, in its answers' own words; C) A Block card: For, Takes in, Done when, How far, Next move; then one row per Question. Leaning: the Block card (ui-draft-v7). Still open: Is "Next move" enough to answer "what do I do now"?
slides.content:
Headline (top-left, large): "Keep one screen: the Block card?"
Three option cards across the middle, joined by a wavy line:
 Card A, label "Mind map": a small branching tree of circles; caption "how it is built"
 Card B, label "Findings": an open notebook with quote marks; caption "what it found"
 Card C, label "Block card", circled with a thick orange marker loop and a small hand-written tag "leaning": a card with five short ruled lines and a small arrow at the bottom marked "next move"; caption "one card, then a row per Question"
Bottom-right mustard sticky note with a big question mark: "Still open: is the next move enough?"
Focal point: card C.

slides.idea: How big may a Studio grow?
slides.notes: Options: A) No limit: every thought gets a topic; B) A cap per level: Block 10, Job 3, Task 2; C) One topic per open question; closed topics fold away. Still open: Is a cap a rule, or only a warning?
slides.content:
Headline (top-left, large): "How big may a Studio grow?"
Three option cards across the middle, joined by a wavy line, all the same weight (no favourite yet):
 Card A, label "No limit": an overflowing pile of sticky notes; caption "every thought gets a topic"
 Card B, label "A cap": three jars marked "10", "3", "2"; caption "Block, Job, Task"
 Card C, label "One per question": a short row of open cards and a small drawer holding folded ones; caption "closed topics fold away"
Bottom-right mustard sticky note with a big question mark: "Still open: is a cap a rule or a warning?"
Focal point: the headline, then the three cards evenly.
